summary: linux-clippy gets its own skip-policy entry (shadow, enforce false) keyed by exactly what the clippy stage reads, with the base's clippy-baseline as a base input the verifier computes; its gate job runs beside linux-gate's, and linux-clippy's own run of the clippy stage (scripts/ci-clippy-keyed, CI's linux-clippy job) warns when cargo read a file the key does not cover (scripts/dep-info-check --warn, while in shadow); linux-gate's run of the same stage does not read the policy, so it keeps its per-check CI inputs

replay.detail: No record, signature or storage format changes; CI's clippy stage note records one more input, clippy_base_baseline_sha256.

schema.detail: The skip policy accepts base_inputs on a kind: an input name mapped to a path whose sha256 at the accepted base a note must have recorded. A policy without it reads as before.

rules.detail: Shadow only: the linux-clippy gate never says skip while enforce is false. linux-clippy's run of the clippy stage (CI's linux-clippy job and scripts/ci-clippy-keyed) also warns, without failing, when its compiles read a repository file outside linux-clippy's inputs; linux-gate's local run of the stage does not check it.

compatibility.detail: Existing notes and checks are unchanged; linux-gate still covers clippy as before.

recovery.detail: Revert the change; the shadow entry and gate job go with it.
